judgments.evidence: src/trace.jl:22-25 tags a record by writer index into trace.schemas, and the harness writer is a schema entry (src/sim.jl:2671 drains plane.harness_drain into the same trace). Probe P3 (probe.jl:26) with no device rostered records 300 batches whose only writer tag is "harness".
judgments.fix: The input trace is the sequence of drained, writer-tagged batches per frame, each batch tagged by the device or the harness writer that staged it.
judgments.note: This is a wording issue. The harness writer is not a device (glossary g-harness-writer), but its batches are recorded and replayed like a device's. The glossary entry g-trace (spec.md:17118) repeats "device-tagged".

judgments.evidence: src/trace.jl:121-133. _record! runs two passes over the mask, one to count and one to fill, so the cost is O(width). It allocates one entries vector at its final length per drained batch and boxes the values into it.
judgments.note: The code makes two O(width) passes, not one. The order of cost the doc states still holds.

judgments.evidence: src/sim.jl:848-856. init!(sim.model, …) runs boundary zero and publishes through settled!, then trc.header = Checkpoint(checkpoint(sim.model), …). Probe P1 (probe.jl:14) gives a header with frame 0 and boundary 1, so it was taken after the first publication.
src/checkpoint.jl:85-96. ModelState also has a `stepper` field, the stepper's carried state. Probe P4 (probe.jl:29) prints (:x, :s, :m, :table, :prior, :stepper, :t, :t₀, :deployment, :layout).
judgments.fix: A checkpoint holds the flat buffer `x`, the `s` and `m` stores, the whole signal table (the collection of cells holding every produced signal), the guard priors, the stepper's carried state, `t` and `t₀`, the frame and boundary counters, and the fingerprint (the structural layout) and the deployment ([D-319][d-319], [D-452][d-452]).
judgments.note: The move is recorded in the D-274 annotation of 2026-11-11 (log.md:12433-12436), in D-452, in commit e7dacf9e, and in §12.6's list (spec.md:10629).

judgments.evidence: src/deployment.jl:539-553 has no policy field; probe P5 (probe.jl:32) confirms this. t_end and ignore_stop_requests are keywords of run!, step! and replay!, bound per call by _bind_policy (src/sim.jl:474, 1386, 1488).
